questions.prompt: How does the expense tracker divide its work between App, Expense, ExpenseManager and ExpenseFileStorage? Say what App handles and what it delegates, why validation and reporting live in ExpenseManager and where that class sits, what the storage class knows and does not know, what makes Expense immutable, and the beginner lesson the structure teaches.

keyPoints.text: App shows the menu, reads input, prints results and catches invalid input with friendly messages.
keyPoints.quote: catching invalid input and showing friendly messages

keyPoints.text: Totals, filtering, rule validation and file details are delegated to other classes.
keyPoints.quote: Those jobs are delegated to other classes.

keyPoints.text: Validation and reporting belong in ExpenseManager because they are about the app's behavior, not the menu.
keyPoints.quote: This is where validation and reporting logic belong, because those rules are about the app's behavior, not about the menu.

keyPoints.text: ExpenseManager is the middle layer between the CLI and the stored data.
keyPoints.quote: `ExpenseManager` is the middle layer between the CLI and the stored data.

keyPoints.text: The storage class knows how to turn an Expense into a line of text and back.
keyPoints.quote: how to turn an `Expense` into a line of text

keyPoints.text: It knows nothing about menu choices or user interaction.
keyPoints.quote: It does not know anything about menu choices or user interaction.

keyPoints.text: Expense is immutable after creation because all its fields are final.
keyPoints.quote: It is immutable after creation because all fields are `final`.

keyPoints.text: The lesson: not all code belongs in main; one giant method would be hard to read and change.
keyPoints.quote: not all code belongs in `main`.

questions.prompt: Why does the expense tracker save to a tab-separated plain-text file rather than JSON or CSV? Give the reasons for the choice, the tradeoff against JSON, against CSV and of plain text itself, and the principle that settles it.

keyPoints.text: It is easy to open and inspect in a text editor.
keyPoints.quote: it is easy to open and inspect in a text editor

keyPoints.text: Java can read and write it with built-in classes, so no frameworks or libraries are added.
keyPoints.quote: Java can read and write it with built-in classes

keyPoints.text: JSON is more standard for nested data but more work without a library.
keyPoints.quote: JSON is more standard for nested data, but it is more work without a library

keyPoints.text: CSV is common, but proper CSV escaping rules can confuse a beginner.
keyPoints.quote: CSV is common, but proper CSV escaping rules can be confusing for a beginner

keyPoints.text: Plain text is simple and readable but less standardized.
keyPoints.quote: plain text is simple and readable, but less standardized

keyPoints.text: For this project, learnability matters more than perfection.
keyPoints.quote: For this project, learnability matters more than perfection.

questions.prompt: Walk through how the expense tracker saves and loads. When is the file written and by which call, what does the storage class do step by step when saving, and what does it do when loading, including when the file is missing and which lines it ignores?

keyPoints.text: On exit, App.saveExpenses calls ExpenseFileStorage.save.
keyPoints.quote: When the app exits, `App.saveExpenses` calls `ExpenseFileStorage.save`.

keyPoints.text: Saving creates the data directory if needed.
keyPoints.quote: creates the `data` directory if needed

keyPoints.text: It writes a small header comment, then one expense per line.
keyPoints.quote: writes a small header comment

keyPoints.text: On start, App.loadExpenses calls ExpenseFileStorage.load.
keyPoints.quote: When the app starts, `App.loadExpenses` calls `ExpenseFileStorage.load`.

keyPoints.text: If the file does not exist, load returns an empty list.
keyPoints.quote: if it does not exist, returns an empty list

keyPoints.text: It skips comments and blank lines.
keyPoints.quote: skips comments and blank lines

keyPoints.text: Each expense line is parsed into an Expense and the list goes to the manager.
keyPoints.quote: parses each expense line into an `Expense`
